2608.10692.title: SPIEval: Evaluating Large Language Models as Mobile Assistants over Scattered Personal Information
2608.10692.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as mobile assistants, where a key challenge is leveraging personal information scattered across multiple applications (apps) to complete user instructions. However, due to the lack of dedicated benchmarks, their capabilities remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we introduce SPIEval, a human-curated benchmark grounded in five cognitive capabilities (i.e., reasoning, disambiguation, integration, preference inference, and multi-intent decomposition). SPIEval comprises 250 tasks spanning 4,335 personal records distributed across 10 apps and supports multi-turn interaction through 21 tools. Analysis shows that the benchmark exhibits diverse scenarios, challenging tasks, scattered information, controllable environments, and verifiable outcomes. We evaluate nine representative LLMs and find substantial room for improvement. The best-performing model, GPT-5.5 (xhigh), achieves only 57.3% accuracy, while the weakest achieves just 16.4%. Further analysis reveals that 79% of failures stem from inaccurate information localization, as LLMs often commit to plausible but incorrect information instead of continuing retrieval for verification. We also find that fewer than 2% of retrieval actions employ advanced search methods and observe substantial variation in search efficiency across models. These findings expose fundamental limitations of current LLM-based mobile assistants and motivate future research in this direction. Data and code are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Junjie-Ye/SPIEval.
2608.10692.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地被用作行動助手，其中一個主要挑戰是利用散佈在多個應用程式（apps）中的個人資訊來完成用戶指令。<lb/>然而，由於缺乏專門的基準，這些模型的能力仍然不甚了解。<lb/>為了解決這一差距，我們引入了SPIEval，一個基於五種認知能力（即推理、消歧、整合、偏好推斷和多意圖分解）的人為策劃基準。<lb/>SPIEval包含250個任務，涵蓋了分佈在10個應用程式中的4,335條個人記錄，並通過21個工具支持多輪互動。<lb/>分析顯示，該基準展現了多樣的場景、具有挑戰性的任務、分散的信息、可控的環境和可驗證的結果。<lb/>我們評估了九個具有代表性的LLM，發現仍有相當大的改進空間。<lb/>表現最佳的模型GPT-5.5（xhigh）僅達到57.3%的準確率，而表現最差的僅為16.4%。<lb/>進一步分析顯示，79%的失敗源於不準確的信息定位，因為LLMs經常堅持於似是而非但不正確的信息，而不是繼續檢索以進行驗證。<lb/>我們還發現，少於2%的檢索行動使用了先進的搜索方法，並觀察到不同模型之間的搜索效率有顯著變化。<lb/>這些發現揭示了當前基於LLM的行動助手的基本限制，並激勵未來在這一方向的研究。<lb/>數據和代碼可在https://huggingface.co/datasets/Junjie-Ye/SPIEval獲得。
